rounds.text: The most concerning aspect of R.K. Fashion Accessories Ltd is the severe disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation. Despite high growth figures, the company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.68 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -1.34 Cr for March 2026 [E20, E21]. This results in a concerning cash conversion ratio of -0.11x, suggesting that the company’s earnings are not being effectively translated into liquidity [E19]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is deteriorating, as evidenced by debtor days increasing from 28.9 to 41.1 and working capital days ballooning from 32.6 to 89.9 [E33, E34]. The significant reduction in promoter shareholding from 99.66% to 72.26% in a single month also warrants caution regarding management's long-term commitment [E25]. Conceded: the company maintains strong return ratios, including an ROE of 37.1% and an ROCE of 50.4% [E11, E12]. However, these metrics are undermined by inconsistent operating margins over the last three years and two quarters, indicating a lack of stability in the underlying business model [E17, E18].
